note: Neither depends on the other. ERC-8004 publishes x402Support, uses agentWallet as the payee address, and lets feedback files carry proofOfPayment for an x402 payment; Erik Reppel co-authors ERC-8004 and sits on the x402 TSC.

The MPP payment discovery draft cites ERC-8004 without specifying an integration. Since mppx 0.20.0 (2026-11-16), MPP's reference SDK ships an ERC-8004 identity provider: the server reads getAgentWallet from the Identity Registry (on Tempo mainnet by default) and accepts a request, or a tempo charge, signed by that wallet. It is an SDK feature, not part of ERC-8004 or of an MPP draft.

Indirect only: ERC-8004 lists A2A agent cards as services and AP2 can be implemented as an A2A extension. ERC-8226 defines an on-chain mandate comparable to an AP2 mandate; neither references the other.
